analysis.title: S&P 500 Futures: What Stops the Selling?
key_insights: Commitment of Traders data through September 29th show continued Non-Dealer S&P 500 futures selling. Non-Dealers sold $10.5bn from September 22nd-29th, the 5th week of selling in the past 6 since August 18th, for a net -$63.7bn.
Shorts dominated the latest release, though long unwinds accounted for more than 70% of the selling across the 1.5 month window.
Asset Managers led the selling, at $11.7bn in the latest report, with Other selling $1.1bn. Hedge Funds and Non-Reportable bought $620mm and $1.6bn respectively.
Higher real rates and/or quarterly rebalancing provided overhangs. Asset Manager liquidation equaled $5.5bn, coinciding with a 25bp jump in US 10 year real yields.
The rolling 3 month correlation between Asset Manager gross longs and USGGT10Y Index moved well into negative territory. Proximity to quarter-end suggests asset reallocation may have started early.

Lower probabilities of imminent Fed hikes boosted equities. Below-consensus PCE, dovish Fed speakers and a miss on Nonfarm payrolls reduced October hike pricing, enabling a 0.70% recovery in the S&P index.
Deferred real rates rose marginally: the December Adjusted Interest Rate future, a funding proxy, cheapened by about 5bps. GS argues S&P futures flows therefore remained arguably bearish.
Asset Manager net length stood at a 77% 2 year rank on September 29th, before additional probable sales. GS expects ongoing challenges until yields convincingly reverse.
GS rates research sees recent developments and valuation as presenting a clearer skew toward lower yields, despite upward pressure from oil and the resilience of AI investment plans.
